arxiv-2001-10517.title: Quantum Computation and Arrows of Time
arxiv-2001-10517.creator: Nathan Argaman
arxiv-2001-10517.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Nathan Argaman. Quantum physics is surprising in many ways. One surprise is the threat to locality implied by Bell’s Theorem. Another surprise is the capacity of quantum computation, which poses a threat to the complexity-theoretic Church-Turing thesis. In both cases, the surprise may be due to taking for granted a certain strict arrow-of-time assumption, whose applicability may be limited to the classical domain. This possibility has been noted repeatedly in the context of Bell’s Theorem. The argument concerning quantum computation is described here.

arxiv-2012-05915.title: Symmetry constraints on superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene: Fractional vortices, 4 ​ e 4e condensates or non-unitary pairing
arxiv-2012-05915.creator: Eslam Khalaf, Patrick Ledwith, Ashvin Vishwanath
arxiv-2012-05915.description: Abstract When two graphene sheets are twisted relative to each other by a small angle, enhanced correlations lead to superconductivity whose origin remains under debate. Here, we derive some general constraints on superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG), independent of its underlying mechanism.

arxiv-2103-09189.title: Goal-constrained Sparse Reinforcement Learning for End-to-End Driving
arxiv-2103-09189.creator: Pranav Agarwal, Pierre de Beaucorps, Raoul de Charette
arxiv-2103-09189.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pranav Agarwal, Pierre de Beaucorps, Raoul de Charette. Deep reinforcement Learning for end-to-end driving is limited by the need of complex reward engineering. Sparse rewards can circumvent this challenge but suffers from long training time and leads to sub-optimal policy. In this work, we explore full-control driving with only goal-constrained sparse reward and propose a curriculum learning approach for end-to-end driving using only navigation view maps that benefit from small virtual-to-real domain gap.

arxiv-2103-15470.title: Dual-Parameterized Quantum Circuit GAN Model in High Energy Physics
arxiv-2103-15470.creator: \firstname Su Yeon \lastname Chang \fnsep, \firstname Steven \lastname Herbert \fnsep, \firstname Sofia \lastname Vallecorsa \fnsep, \firstname Elías F. \lastname Combarro, \firstname Ross \lastname Duncan

It has been proposed that, in certain circumstances, simulation using GANs can be sped-up by using quantum GANs (qGANs).

arxiv-2301-01893.title: GIVL: Improving Geographical Inclusivity of Vision-Language Models with Pre-Training Methods
arxiv-2301-01893.creator: Da Yin, Feng Gao, Govind Thattai, Michael Johnston, Kai-Wei Chang
arxiv-2301-01893.description: Abstract A key goal for the advancement of AI is to develop technologies that serve the needs not just of one group but of all communities regardless of their geographical region. In fact, a significant proportion of knowledge is locally shared by people from certain regions but may not apply equally in other regions because of cultural differences.

arxiv-2307-01877.title: Fast Private Kernel Density Estimation via Locality Sensitive Quantization
arxiv-2307-01877.creator: Tal Wagner, Yonatan Naamad, Nina Mishra
arxiv-2307-01877.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tal Wagner, Yonatan Naamad, Nina Mishra. We study efficient mechanisms for differentially private kernel density estimation (DP-KDE). Prior work for the Gaussian kernel described algorithms that run in time exponential in the number of dimensions d d . This paper breaks the exponential barrier, and shows how the KDE can privately be approximated in time linear in d d , making it feasible for high-dimensional data. We also present improved bounds for low-dimensional data.

arxiv-2401-01384.title: Strong Transitivity Relations and Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2401-01384.creator: Yassin Mohamadi, Mostafa Haghir Chehreghani
arxiv-2401-01384.description: Abstract Abstract Local neighborhoods play a crucial role in embedding generation in graph-based learning. It is commonly believed that nodes ought to have embeddings that resemble those of their neighbors. In this research, we try to carefully expand the concept of similarity from nearby neighborhoods to the entire graph.

arxiv-2405-14416.title: VelCrys: Interactive web-based application to compute acoustic wave velocity in crystals and its magnetic corrections
arxiv-2405-14416.creator: P. Nieves, I. Korniienko, A. Fraile, J.M. Fernández, R. Iglesias, D. Legut
arxiv-2405-14416.description: Abstract We present VelCrys, a web-based interactive tool, that allows to perform further post-processing of the elastic tensor in order to compute and plot the group velocity of the acoustic waves for any crystal symmetry. We also implemented the calculation of effective magnetic corrections to the elastic tensor and corresponding fractional change in group velocity under a magnetic field.

arxiv-2406-02908.title: The HS-CMU Dataset for Diagnosing Benign and Malignant Diseases through Hysteroscopy
arxiv-2406-02908.creator: Ruxue Han 1 , Yuantao Xie 2 , Kangze You 2 , Lijun Cao 2 , Hua Li 1
arxiv-2406-02908.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ruxue Han 1 , Yuantao Xie 2 , Kangze You 2 , Lijun Cao 2 , Hua Li 1. Hysteroscopy enables direct visualization of morphological changes in the endometrium, serving as an important means for screening, diagnosing, and treating intrauterine lesions. Accurate identification of the benign or malignant nature of diseases is crucial. However, the complexity and variability of uterine morphology increase the difficulty of identification, leading to missed diagnoses and misdiagnoses, often requiring the expertise of experienced gynecologists and pathologists.

arxiv-2506-04288.title: Backbone Augmented Training for Adaptations
arxiv-2506-04288.creator: Jae Wan Park, Junhyeok Kim, Youngjun Jun, Hyunah Ko, Seong Jae Hwang
arxiv-2506-04288.description: Abstract Adaptations facilitate efficient training of large backbone models, including diffusion models for image generation and transformer-based language models. While various adaptation techniques enhance performance with minimal computational resources, limited adaptation data often lead to challenges in training. To address this, we focus on the enormous amount of backbone data used to pre-train the backbone models.

arxiv-2506-20754.title: Domain Knowledge in Requirements Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study
arxiv-2506-20754.creator: Marina Araújo, Júlia Araújo, Romeu Oliveira, Lucas Romao, Marcos Kalinowski
arxiv-2506-20754.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marina Araújo, Júlia Araújo, Romeu Oliveira, Lucas Romao, Marcos Kalinowski. Domain knowledge is recognized as a key component for the success of Requirements Engineering (RE), as it provides the conceptual support needed to understand the system context, ensure alignment with stakeholder needs, and reduce ambiguity in requirements specification. Despite its relevance, the scientific literature still lacks a systematic consolidation of how domain knowledge can be effectively used and operationalized in RE.

arxiv-2510-06874.title: Quantized Dirac Fields in torsionful gravity: cosmological implications and links with the dark universe
arxiv-2510-06874.creator: Antonio Capolupo, Sante Carloni, Luca Fabbri, Simone Monda, Aniello Quaranta, Stefano Vignolo
arxiv-2510-06874.description: Abstract We consider a classical field in square torsion theory as a source of torsion for a quantum fermion field in FLRW metric. In the framework of QFT, we obtain vacuum contributions to the energy-momentum tensor and to the axial current that modify the dynamics of the classical field and the field equations as back-reaction.

pmc-10606254.title: LRP5, Bone Mass Polymorphisms and Skeletal Disorders
pmc-10606254.creator: Jake Littman, Wentian Yang, Jon Olansen, Chanika Phornphutkul, Roy K Aaron, David N Cooper, Zhousheng Xiao
pmc-10606254.description: The formation and maintenance of the gross structure and microarchitecture of the human skeleton require the concerted functioning of a plethora of morphogenic signaling processes. pmc-11494009.title: In the arm-in-cage test, topical repellents activate mosquitoes to disengage upon contact instead of repelling them at distance
pmc-11494009.creator: Mathurin Fatou, Pie Müller
pmc-11494009.description: Topical repellents provide protection against mosquito bites and their efficacy is often assessed using the arm-in-cage test. The arm-in-cage test estimates the repellent’s protection time by exposing a repellent-treated forearm to host-seeking mosquitoes inside a cage at regular intervals until the first confirmed mosquito bite. However, the test does not reveal the repellents’ behavioural mode of action.

pmc-12612059.title: Physiological indicators drive climate-smart and sustainable AWD irrigation in rice systems
pmc-12612059.creator: Bittawat Wichaidist, Amornrat Intrman, Pavit Junhom, Songsak Puttrawutichai, Chawakorn Rewtragulpaibul, Chaisri Suksaroj
pmc-12612059.description: Efficient water management is crucial for modern rice cultivation, particularly in the context of climate change and limited water resources. To optimize irrigation, this study evaluated the physiological responses of rice to water stress. From January to April 2022, a randomized complete block design (RCBD) was employed to evaluate physiological traits associated with water regulation in rice plants.

pmc-13597489.description: Anorexia nervosa (AN) involves limbic dysfunction, yet its neurobiology remains unclear. We hypothesized that subcortical limbic volumes would be reduced in AN, normalize partially following short-term weight-restoration, and fully after long-term recovery.

uslaw-usc-t31-s6707.title: 31 U.S.C. § 6707 — State variation of local government allocations
uslaw-usc-t31-s6707.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t31-s6707.description: United States Code, Title 31 (Money And Finance); Chapter 67 (Federal Payments). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) State Formula.— A State government may provide by law for the allocation of amounts among units of general local government in the State on the basis of population multiplied by the general tax effort factors or income gaps of the units of general local.
